title: EmailAddress.address: Option<String> forces every caller to defend against None for malformed entries that should be filtered out
description:
header_typed.rs:40-46 — EmailAddress has `pub address: Option<String>`. The doc says "Both are populated best-effort; either may be `None` if the original header is malformed."

In practice, an EmailAddress with `address: None` is unusable:
- A caller wanting to send mail cannot do anything with it.
- A caller wanting to compare addresses (e.g., dedup by addr-spec) cannot key the comparison.
- A caller surfacing it in UI shows only the display name, which may also be None.

Every caller therefore writes:

    for e in addresses {
        let Some(addr) = e.address else { continue; };
        // ... real work ...
    }

The defensive boilerplate is the contract: an EmailAddress with no address is filler. Either the type should reflect that (address: String, required) and parse_header_typed should filter address-less entries, or the doc should explain a real use case for keeping them.

Caller-facing consequence: every consumer writes the same is_some check or filter_map. For JMAP, RFC 8621 §4.1.2.3 says the EmailAddress object has both `name: String|null` and `email: String|null` to mirror raw mailbox structure faithfully — but JMAP servers always filter or coalesce in practice.

Inspection of convert_addr (header_typed.rs:281-302) shows address is None only when mail-parser's parse_address produces an Addr with no `address` field. This happens for severely malformed input.

Fix options:

a) Change `address: Option<String>` → `address: String`. Drop entries where mail-parser produced no address in parse_header_typed's Addresses/GroupedAddresses arms.

b) Keep Option but document a concrete use case ("display-name-only mailboxes from non-spec-conformant mail like Outlook drafts are preserved as address: None") and add a method `EmailAddress::is_addressable(&self) -> bool` that callers can use without manual destructuring.

Either is a contract improvement. Status quo is defensive-code-forcing.

Note: same concern applies to EmailAddress.name (Option), but a name-less mailbox IS legitimate and useful (the bare addr-spec), so name's Optional-ness is justified. address's is not.
close_reason: Final API additions: (.14) Added EmailAddress::is_addressable() helper; keeps the Option<String> address field but eliminates the defensive is_some() boilerplate at every call site. Doctest demonstrates the filter pattern. (.28) Added HeaderForm::Text and HeaderValueTyped::Text(String) implementing RFC 8621 §4.1.2.2 — whitespace unfold, RFC 2047 decode (via mail-parser's parse_unstructured), NFC normalisation (via new unicode-normalization dep). parse_text helper, asText accepted by FromStr and emitted by Display. Module-level table now lists all 7 RFC 8621 forms. Tests cover RFC 2047 decode and NFD->NFC normalisation. (.29) Fixed misleading module doc that directed callers at ParsedPart::header_range slicing; the natural path is header.value.as_bytes(). Added parse_header_typed_from(&ParsedHeader, HeaderForm) convenience helper that wraps that pattern.
